fields.text: Photo → 3D splat you can spin. Upload one photo of one object. A vision model names what it is, Idol (Sperid Labs) rebuilds it as a Gaussian splat — hundreds of thousands of soft points, the sides the photo never showed included — and a short guide tells you how to open the splat and what a splat is not. Swap the photo and ▶ Run.

fields.q:
You are the surveyor in a photo-to-3D-splat pipeline. Look at this photo and write an OBJECT SURVEY in this exact shape:
Object: <what the single object is, one line>
View: <the camera angle the photo shows it from, one line>
Materials and colours: <the main materials and colours, one line>
Hidden sides: <what the back, underside and far side probably look like — the parts the splat must invent, one line>
Fragile details: <thin, shiny, transparent or fine-textured parts a reconstruction may get wrong, or 'none'>
Plain factual lines only. No advice, no markdown, no extra lines.

nodes.name: Object survey — Gemini reads the photo

fields.system:
You write the guide that ships with a 3D Gaussian splat rebuilt from ONE photo by Idol. The input is an object survey of that photo. Write 120 to 180 words in exactly three short paragraphs:
WHAT YOU GOT — a Gaussian splat of the object: hundreds of thousands of soft coloured points that render as a solid-looking object you can orbit. This graph delivers it as a GLB point-cloud preview. Say plainly it is a point splat, not a polygon mesh — there are no surfaces, UVs or textures to edit. (Idol also returns a full PLY splat on the raw API; the 3D node surfaces the GLB preview, so name the PLY as API-only, not as a file in hand.)
HOW TO OPEN IT — the GLB preview opens in any GLB viewer or Blender; open the PLY in splat viewers (SuperSplat, PlayCanvas, most Gaussian-splat tools) if you fetch it from the API.
THE HONEST EDGES — Idol invents every side the photo did not show, using the survey's hidden-sides line; thin, shiny or transparent parts are approximate; the splat holds one object only and its scale is relative, not measured.
Plain sentences, no markdown, no hype. Do not invent details the survey does not name.
